paper_metadata.title: Empowering Credit Scoring Systems with Quantum-Enhanced Machine Learning

summary: The paper proposes Systemic Quantum Score (SQS), a simulator-only gate-based quantum kernel search for Fintonic credit default prediction using 2-10 qubits. Reported results show normalized fitness values around 0.973-0.998 across kernel configurations, and AUC 0.658 for SQS versus 0.638 for SVC and 0.632 for XGBoost in the scarce-data generalization split, while XGBoost is stated to catch up and outperform on the full dataset.

experiments.description: Systemic Quantum Score (SQS): evolutionary search over quantum kernel feature maps for credit default prediction on Fintonic loan-risk data, evaluated on downsampled datasets and a scarce-data generalization split.

algorithm.variant: evolutionary-discovered quantum kernel / quantum feature map for QSVC-style classification
algorithm.ansatz: Pauli-word feature map with Hadamard initialization and data-encoded Pauli rotations
algorithm.optimizer: gradient-based local optimization within an evolutionary algorithm; evolutionary selection/crossover/mutation
algorithm.convergence_criteria: stop when maximumGenerations reached or bestFitness >= targetFitness

hyperparameters.maximumGenerations: reported as up to 50 in experiments
hyperparameters.targetFitness: reported as input to Algorithm 1; value not specified
hyperparameters.geneChainSize: reported as input to Algorithm 1; value not specified
hyperparameters.crossover: reported as input to Algorithm 1; value not specified
hyperparameters.mutationPercentage: reported as input to Algorithm 1; value not specified
hyperparameters.eliteSize: reported as input to Algorithm 1; value not specified
hyperparameters.quantumDim: final dataset dimension aligned with selected qubit amount; up to 10
hyperparameters.train_test_split: 20% test set for kernel evaluation; separate 10% train / 90% test generalization experiment
hyperparameters.dimensionality_reduction: LDA + standardization to fit quantum feature map

algorithm.parameter_initialization: initial population randomly generated; alpha parameters randomly initialized then locally optimized at end of each generation

problem_formulation.encoding_details: classical features are first reduced to 10 selected features, then reduced further with LDA/standardization to a quantumDim matching the qubit count; data encoded via Pauli-word rotations in the feature map
problem_formulation.objective_function: maximize kernel target alignment / normalized eigenvalue fitness against ideal target kernel K* = yy^T
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: none reported beyond feature selection and dimensionality reduction to fit simulator tractability

problem_instance.description: Binary credit default prediction for Fintonic/Wanna loan-risk model using aggregated banking information over the prior 3 months

dataset_specification.description: 4763 loans from 2017-2023; about 10% positive class (defaulters); 20% test split for kernel experiments; 10% train / 90% test for generalization study

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: duplicate transaction removal, missing-field imputation, feature engineering with featuretools/deep feature synthesis, mutual-information feature selection, LDA dimensionality reduction, standardization, downsampling for scalability experiments
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: kernel evaluation on 20% test set; comparison across subsampled dataset sizes; generalization test with 10% training and 90% testing; metrics reported include normalized fitness and AUC

implementation_details.classical_solver: XGBoost baseline; SVC baseline; kernel alignment / evolutionary search for quantum feature maps
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: AUC and normalized fitness comparison across models

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not report computational speedup, asymptotic complexity, or runtime comparisons. It only claims improved predictive performance/generalization in scarce-data regimes.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: A gate-based quantum kernel implementation with up to 10 qubits, evaluated only on simulators; no hardware resource scaling or runtime advantage data reported.
limiting_factors: performance advantage limited to scarce-data regimes
classical XGBoost remains better on the full dataset
classical SVC is close in AUC

notes: Paper explicitly states the whole procedure was performed under simulators and that execution on real hardware was unexplored.
No specific simulator type, framework, shot count, gate counts, or transpiled depth are reported.
The paper reports a quantum-kernel approach and compares against classical baselines, but does not characterize an asymptotic speedup order.
The paper claims improved predictive performance for SQS in scarce-data settings, but does not demonstrate computational quantum advantage.
On the full dataset, XGBoost outperforms SQS; SQS only leads in the downsampled and scarce-data regime.
